chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Qutayba al-A'sha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Three handfuls of dry Suweyq (flour soup) on an empty stomach dries the phlegm and the bile until it almost leaves nothing.

key_terms.سَوِيق: Suweyq, a traditional flour-based soup or porridge

ai.seo_question: What is the health benefit of eating dry Suweyq on an empty stomach according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes three handfuls of dry Suweyq (roasted flour) on an empty stomach as a potent remedy to desiccate excess phlegm and bile, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of utilizing simple, accessible foods for preventive medicine. This recommendation aligns with the Shia emphasis on *Tibb al-Nabawi* (Prophetic Medicine), where dietary moderation and specific food properties are viewed as essential components of maintaining physical and spiritual purity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Quteyba Al A’ash, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Three handfuls of dry Suweyq upon the empty stomach dries the phlegm, and the bile until it almost leaves nothing’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Qutaybah al-‘A’sha’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Three handfuls of dry sawiq before breakfast absorbs phlegm and bile and it almost does not leave anything behind.’”
